gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2025. GDP 187,933,316,143 2011 int$ (World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD rebased x 0.8005) / population 4,865,298 = 38,627 2011 int$. Range +/-10%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank: 4.69% of GDP in 2025, 4.44% 2024, 4.28% 2023 (low). High allows for 2026 wartime spending.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction (and hydrocarbons) 54.1% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS). Range +/-7% for oil-price swings.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.0 -> 0.84. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/KWT/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 1.89% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.11 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.11-0.12). Mid 1 - 0.019/0.11 = 0.84. Low: a x 1.5 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.11 = 0.73. High: s 0.12 = 0.84. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 11% of domestic calorie supply. a includes expatriate farm labour. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Imports nearly all food.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 2,971,432 x share of males aged 15-19 4.789% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 28,462. Male population from SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN. Males only (conscript-pool convention). Range +/-10% for single-year cohort variation. Includes expatriate youths.

railKm.note: CIA Factbook lists no railways; the GCC railway link is unbuilt.

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 6 ports, 0 large, 2 medium; key ports Ash Shuaybah, Ash Shuwaykh, Mina al Ahmadi, Mina Abd Allah, Mina Su'ud, Doha.

merchantTonnage.note: asOf 2025: 4,739 thousand DWT under the Kuwaiti flag (2,708 thousand GT), mostly KOTC tankers.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Small country; little expeditionary logistics.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Camels; not from FAO data.

nuclearWarheads.note: Kuwait is not listed among the nine nuclear-armed states in the FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces 2026 table.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.0-1.1: flat desert with no depth (overrun in 1990 in two days).

notes: WARTIME snapshot: struck by Iran during the 2026 Iran war (4 soldiers killed, war article). asOf 2025 economic data, 2026 order of battle. Population: all residents inside ne:KWT, ~70% expatriates; the mobilization ratio is set low for that reason. Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Counts from the Kuwait Land Forces, Air Force and Navy articles; several Air Force counts are blank on the page and bracketed. Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). National Guard (7,100) excluded as paramilitary; US forces at Camp Arifjan not counted.
